- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments after sharp spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — correct by adding 1–2 days of downward bias.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to 30-day moving average — adjust forecast by subtracting 0.5–1.5% of recent peak from forecasted values.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early weeks of a trend — reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with true momentum.
- Sentiment-driven volatility: when sentiment swings sharply (±0.40+), model overreacts — dampen forecast volatility by 20–30% in such periods.
